diagrams.title: Five Steps to Board a Merchant Without Leaving Money on the Table
diagrams.subtitle: From free cost analysis to clean gateway billing

stages.label: Run a free cost analysis
stages.detail: Transaction Expert says any merchant without a cost analysis in the last 12 months may still be funding a processor's Durbin windfall.

stages.label: Pull the average ticket
stages.detail: Under $10 the 22-cent per-item fee raises costs, while around $30 and above the Durbin cap actually saves money.

stages.label: Verify SIC/MCC and card-present setup
stages.detail: Bryan Manning benchmarks about 1.25% to 2% card-present and about 2% to 3.5% card-not-present; miscoding means paying higher rates than the merchant qualifies for.

stages.label: Board at interchange plus 0.25%
stages.detail: James Shepherd boards every new client at interchange plus 0.25% so Durbin cost drops pass through automatically.

stages.label: Resolve past-due gateway billing
stages.detail: NMI moves past-due merchants to delinquent, and after 6 months of uncollected fees the balance is debited from the affiliate account.

diagrams.caption: Agents who board on interchange plus and verify ticket size and coding first keep Durbin savings flowing to the merchant and protect their own affiliate account.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Step order is an editorial sequence assembled from separate practitioner gates; rate bands are general benchmarks, not quotes.
diagrams.note: Sources include Transaction Expert, James Shepherd (durbinamendment), Bryan Manning of BancardSales, and NMI.

diagrams.title: From One Account to a $10,000 Monthly Residual Book
diagrams.subtitle: Merchant-count milestones reported by working agents

stages.label: Target book with safety buffer
stages.detail: Residual Builders adds 15 to 20 clients on top of the raw count to absorb shortfalls and cancels.

stages.label: Core clients at $400 each
stages.detail: Residual Builders models $300 to $400 per client when planning a $10,000 monthly target.

stages.label: Twenty-sale milestone
stages.detail: James Shepard's average across agents selling for North American Bank Card and Total Merchant Services.

stages.label: Ten-sale milestone
stages.detail: Shepard benchmarks an industry-average split of about 50% and about $275 average upfront.

stages.label: First active account
stages.conversion: Paid roughly two months behind the sale
stages.detail: Electronic Money Company recalls a first residual check of $187; Ryan Anthony pegs accounts at $100 to $500 a month.

diagrams.caption: Residual income compounds one account at a time, and practitioners plan for cancels by over-building the merchant count.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Per-account figures differ by practitioner, from about $30 (Shepard) to $300-$400 (Residual Builders); milestones are not one agent's book.
diagrams.note: Sources include Residual Builders, James Shepard of CCSalesPro, Ryan Anthony, and Electronic Money Company.

diagrams.title: How Enhanced Line Items Pull a Commercial Card Rate Down
diagrams.subtitle: Rate steps in percent of sale for a business-card merchant
diagrams.caption: Sean Jones moved an e-commerce client from rates as high as 3% to about 1.9% at Level 2 and 1.45% on large tickets, saving $35,000 per month.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative overlay of Jones' client rates with TouchSuite's 0.05% CEDP fee; the final 1.5% is arithmetic, and CEDP Verified status is required for Level 3 rates.
diagrams.note: Sources include Sean Jones of Revolution Payments, TouchSuite, and PayTrace, which quotes 75 to 120 bps of Visa commercial savings.

diagrams.title: Effective Rate Yardsticks for Reading Any Statement
diagrams.subtitle: Benchmarks practitioners use to spot overpaying merchants

bars.label: Coffee shop flat rate that lost money

diagrams.caption: Total interchange divided by volume should land near 1.7%, and total fees minus interchange exposes the real markup.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The 1.7% average was stated as of May 2019; single-point bars reflect thresholds quoted without a range.
diagrams.note: Sources include CCSalesPro, Helcim, and Bryan Manning of BancardSales, who calls the effective rate the only undisputed yardstick.

diagrams.title: Four Gates Before Passing Card Fees to Customers
diagrams.subtitle: Compliance checks for surcharging, cash discount, and dual pricing

nodes.question: Is the merchant's effective rate high enough to justify passing the cost on?
nodes.fail_action: Stay on standard pricing, since a low effective rate may not be worth passing on.

nodes.question: Does the terminal or POS block the fee on every debit card, PIN or signature?
nodes.fail_action: Reprogram before launch, because a debit card is a debit card no matter how it is run.

nodes.question: Does every price exist twice on shelves, menus, the website, and quotes?
nodes.fail_action: Fix signage fast; first fines run $1,000, plus $5,000 if not fixed in about 30 to 45 days.

nodes.question: Is any surcharge credit-only, within 3%, with 30 days notice to the acquirer?
nodes.fail_action: Move to dual pricing; a 3.99% card price on $100,000 needs about 3.84% charged to net the merchant zero.

diagrams.caption: The posted price, not the program name, decides which rules apply, which is why James Huber and Ryan Anthony rank dual pricing first.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is editorial; cap levels and customer reaction were disputed among practitioners.
diagrams.note: Sources include Ryan Anthony, POS Nexus, Global Legal Law Firm, and CCSalesPro.

diagrams.title: Who the ATM Operator Negotiates With
diagrams.subtitle: The counterparties behind every signed location

center.focus: Signed location agreements and surcharge pricing near the $3 norm

spokes.kpi: Chad Otsuji held $2 of a $3 surcharge and gave the owner $1
Breach clause bills $4,800 plus a $100 fee on 24 months left
Austin Zaback pays five to ten grand for them to walk
Five self-loaded machines tied up $112,500 for almost 2 years

diagrams.caption: Philip Webb's rule holds across every spoke: no signed location agreement, no machine.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Split, buyout, and breach figures come from different operators and different sites; terms ranged from one-year caps to five-year auto-renewals.
diagrams.note: Sources include Philip Webb, Chad Otsuji ATM Business, and Austin Zaback.

diagrams.title: Average Ticket Decides Whether a Service Fee Stays Above Water
diagrams.subtitle: Signature debit cost as a share of the sale versus the fee charged
diagrams.total_range: Debit cost of about 1% to 6.4% of the sale against a 3% to 3.99% service fee

buckets.label: $5 ticket debit cost
buckets.notes: Fixed 30 to 32 cents swamps the fee; quote a per-item fee such as 59 cents.

buckets.label: $10 ticket debit cost
buckets.notes: Shepherd says a $10 ticket goes negative 20 basis points at 3%.

buckets.label: $30 ticket debit cost
buckets.notes: Inside the $25 to $70 sweet spot with the fattest ISO markup.

buckets.label: Service fee charged
buckets.notes: Corporate reward cards near 2.5% interchange squeeze this on high tickets.

diagrams.caption: Regulated signature debit runs 22 cents plus 5 basis points, roughly 30 to 32 cents all-in, so small tickets sink a percentage fee.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Cost percentages are James Shepherd's examples; FTx POS found over 80% of its card transactions flagged as debit.
diagrams.note: Sources include James Shepherd of CCSalesPro and FTx POS.

diagrams.title: Four-Week Hardware and Vault Cash Launch
diagrams.subtitle: Machine vetting through vaulter controls

weeks.title: Vet the machine
weeks.deliverable: Model number, manufacture date, software version, both passwords and the combo, with EMV and TLS 1.2 as the floor
weeks.gate: Processing company clears the unit before payment

weeks.title: Delivery and programming
weeks.deliverable: Tip indicator checked, clock set to current time, Spanish enabled alongside English where needed

weeks.title: Vault cash plan
weeks.deliverable: Budget $4,200 to $6,200 per week for each busy location
weeks.gate: $16,000 minimum on hand across three busy locations

weeks.title: Vaulter agreement and reconciliation
weeks.deliverable: Signed terms at 70 cents to $1.25 per transaction with fill levels, response times, penalties, and a lead clause
weeks.gate: Daily and monthly reconciliation against settlement deposits

diagrams.caption: The machine is the business and vault cash is the bottleneck, so every step locks down hardware integrity and cash control.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Weekly pacing is an editorial sequence; vault cash needs reflect locations running 283 to 350 transactions.
diagrams.note: Sources include ATMDepot, ATM Connect, Rocket ATM, and Philip Webb.
